items.title: Roy McCurdy interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995
items.q: I met a piano player up there... His name was Roger Fleming.

ctx.x: Because you had Kansas City with that whole era there, and you had Chicago in Capone’s era, and Milt Hinton talks about how much work there was at that point. Now you’re telling us in Alaska.

Oh, yeah. In Alaska there must have been about three, maybe four clubs that had jazz full time. And they were always packed. We played there and when we finished with our duties in the Air Force, I’d go pack up and go into town to play. I’d get home about two in the morning and go back to what I was doing. Yeah. I met a piano player up there. He was out of Baltimore, out of New York actually. His name was Roger Fleming. One of the greatest piano players I had ever heard. And I lost track, I never knew what…
How long were you, a couple of years in the service?
